issues.legal_issue: An order refusing to recognize a claimed statutory right to review finally determines that right and is a judgment appealable under the applicable Letters Patent and court rules.
material_facts: A party applied to review an earlier order quashing an assessment, asserting that a later enactment conferred a statutory right to review.
The single judge dismissed the application because the enactment did not confer that right in the circumstances.
The appellate bench held that the dismissal was not a judgment and therefore was not appealable.
issues.conclusion: The single judge’s order was a judgment under clause 10 of the Letters Patent and Chapter VIII, rule 5 of the court rules; the appellate bench was wrong to hold that no appeal lay.
issues.legal_principle: Under clause 10 of the Letters Patent and Chapter VIII, rule 5, an order is a judgment, even on the narrower approach to that term, when it finally determines a substantive right or liability between the parties. The court considered the approaches in The Justices of the Peace for Calcutta v. The Oriental Gas Co., Hadjee Ismael v. Hadjee Mahommed, Tuljaram v. Alagappa, and Manohar v. Baliram, but found it unnecessary to reconcile them or state a general definition.

predicates.special_appeal_from_single_judge_order: A party seeks a special appeal from an order made by a single judge.
predicates.statutory_review_right_claimed: A party claims that a statute gives it a right to have an earlier decision reviewed.
predicates.order_finally_denies_claimed_right: The order finally rejects the claimed statutory right to review.

issues.definition: When a special appeal challenges a single judge’s order that finally denies a claimed statutory review right, the order is a judgment for purposes of appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory provision requiring review of proceedings under an enactment does not apply to an independent constitutional writ proceeding in which a High Court quashed an assessment.
material_facts: An assessment under the agricultural income-tax legislation was quashed by the High Court in a petition under Article 226 on the ground that the assessing authority lacked jurisdiction.
A later amending enactment validated the assessments and provided for review of specified proceedings under the principal enactment.
The State applied to the High Court to review its writ order under that provision.
The provision directed the court or authority receiving an application to review the proceedings accordingly.
issues.conclusion: The review provision did not apply to the High Court’s Article 226 proceeding, which was an independent original proceeding and not a proceeding under, or a continuation of proceedings under, the principal enactment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the amending enactment applies to proceedings under the principal enactment, not to an independent proceeding under Article 226. A writ proceeding is original, though it is a special or extraordinary original jurisdiction distinct from ordinary civil jurisdiction; it is neither appellate nor revisional and is not a continuation of the underlying assessment proceeding. The court relied on Venkataratnam v. Secretary of State for India, Ryots of Garabandha v. The Zamindar of Parlakimedi, Ramayya v. State of Madras, Moulvi Hamid Hassan Nomani v. Banwarilal Roy, Budge Budge Municipality v. Mangru, and Satyanarayanamurthi v. Income-tax Appellate Tribunal. The provision must be read according to its plain wording and consistently with Articles 226 and 245: a State legislature cannot require a High Court to exercise its Article 226 discretion in a particular way. Reading “shall” as “may” would defeat the provision’s purpose; limiting it to proceedings under the enactment avoids conflict with the Constitution.

predicates.constitutional_writ_proceeding: A party brought a proceeding before a High Court seeking relief through its constitutional writ jurisdiction.
predicates.proceeding_is_independent_and_original: The High Court considered the matter in an original proceeding rather than as an appeal, revision, or continuation of the underlying statutory proceeding.
predicates.statute_limits_review_to_proceedings_und: The review statute confines its operation to proceedings under a specified enactment.

issues.definition: If a constitutional writ is an independent original proceeding and the review statute is confined to proceedings under an enactment, the statute’s review process does not apply to that writ proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot, at a very late stage, convert an application brought solely under a statutory review provision into an application under the Code of Civil Procedure when the alternative basis was not previously advanced.
material_facts: The State filed its review application solely under the amending enactment.
It did not seek to amend the application or rely on Order 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure before either level of the High Court.
It first raised the alternative basis in an additional statement of case after the appeal had been argued for some time.
Treating the application under Order 47 would have raised unresolved questions, including timeliness and the availability of review of the writ order.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused to allow the State to convert its application into one under Order 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure and expressed no opinion on the underlying questions that such an application would raise.
issues.legal_principle: A party may not be permitted to change the basis of a review application for the first time at a very late stage, particularly where doing so raises substantial questions that were not previously addressed. The Court did not decide whether Order 47, or section 151, could otherwise support review of an order made under Article 226, whether the application would be timely, or whether the asserted grounds would justify review.

predicates.review_application_proceeding: A party seeks review of an earlier judicial order.
predicates.application_initially_based_only_on_stat: The party presented the review application solely under a statutory review provision.
predicates.alternative_civil_procedure_basis_raised: The party first asks to rely on a civil-procedure review mechanism only at a very late stage of the proceedings.
predicates.alternative_basis_raises_unresolved_ques: The proposed alternative basis would require the court to address substantial questions that had not previously been raised or decided.

issues.definition: A review application presented solely on a statutory basis is not converted to a civil-procedure basis when that alternative is raised very late and would require resolution of substantial unaddressed questions.
